options.text: An enzyme involved in respiration
A structure in the mitochondria
A molecule that is broken down during respiration to release energy
A type of cell that respires

questions.explanation: A respiratory substrate is any organic molecule that can be broken down in respiration to release energy. Glucose is the most common, but lipids, amino acids, and other sugars can also be used.

questions.stem: Which respiratory substrate releases the most energy per gram?

options.text: Glucose
Starch
Lipid (fat)
Protein

questions.explanation: Lipids release the most energy per gram (approximately 39 kJ/g) because they contain a higher proportion of hydrogen atoms and carbon-hydrogen bonds than carbohydrates or proteins.

questions.stem: Why is glucose the preferred respiratory substrate?

options.text: It does not need enzymes to break it down
It is readily available, easily transported in blood, and quickly broken down
It is the largest molecule
It contains the most energy

questions.explanation: Glucose is the preferred substrate because it is soluble (easily transported in blood), readily available from digestion, and can be quickly broken down to release energy.

questions.stem: What must happen to proteins before they can be used as respiratory substrates?

options.text: They must be combined with oxygen
They must be converted to fat first
Nothing, they can be used directly
They must be deaminated - the amino group is removed, and the remainder enters respiration

questions.explanation: Proteins must first be broken down into amino acids, then deaminated (the amino group is removed in the liver, producing urea). The remaining carbon skeleton can then enter the respiratory pathway.

options.text: The speed of breathing
The number of mitochondria in a cell
The ratio of carbon dioxide produced to oxygen consumed during respiration
The total amount of energy released

questions.explanation: The respiratory quotient (RQ) is calculated as CO2 produced divided by O2 consumed. It indicates which substrate is being respired: glucose has an RQ of 1.0, lipids about 0.7.

questions.stem: What is the RQ value for glucose?
questions.explanation: The RQ for glucose is 1.0 because the moles of CO2 produced equal the moles of O2 consumed: C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O (6 CO2 / 6 O2 = 1.0).

questions.stem: When are lipids typically used as a respiratory substrate?

options.text: Only during sleep
During prolonged exercise or fasting when glucose reserves are depleted
Only in plants
Never - only glucose is used

questions.explanation: Lipids are mainly used during prolonged exercise or periods of fasting when glycogen and glucose supplies are running low. They provide more energy per gram but require more oxygen to break down.
